subject: Re: Interested in Redwood GitHub integration for OpenLib

From: Devon Park <devon@openlib.org>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interested in Redwood - GitHub integration for OpenLib

Hi Alex,

Saw Redwood mentioned in a thread on GitHub Actions and tried the free signup. I work on OpenLib (open-source digital library) - we're exploring inference for code snippet summarization and CI-time checks. A couple of quick questions before we book a demo:

- Do you support a GitHub App or Actions-based integration for auto-scanning PRs?
- Any example repos or an SDK for Rust/Python?
- Is it feasible to run inference against private repos in a self-hosted/private deployment?

Happy to hop on a demo - mornings PST work best for me.

Thanks,
Devon Park
Engineering Lead, OpenLib
https://github.com/openlib-org

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Devon Park <devon@openlib.org>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interested in Redwood - GitHub integration for OpenLib

Hi Devon - great to meet you and thanks for trying Redwood!

Short answers up front:
- GitHub integration: yes - teams use both a GitHub App (for repo-level hooks) and a lightweight GitHub Action for CI checks. We have a reference Action that calls the Redwood API and returns annotations for PRs.
- SDKs: Python and TypeScript are first-class; community-contributed Rust examples exist (we can share a starter repo).
- Private repos: supported via Redwood Private (VPC / private deployment) or ephemeral tokens with strict repo-scoped access for hosted customers.

I can walk through the integrations and recommended architecture on a quick call. Here are some times I have open:
- Tue 6/16 10:00-11:00 AM PDT
- Tue 6/16 2:00-3:00 PM PDT
- Wed 6/17 9:00-11:00 AM PDT

Or pick any slot on my calendar: https://calendly.com/alex-martinez/30min

I've attached a one-pager that outlines deployment options and common integration patterns (GitHub App vs Action).

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
SDR, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-one-pager.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:32:00 -0700

Perfect - calendar invite sent for Tue 6/16 10:00 AM PDT (30 min).

Quick notes so your team can prepare:
- GitHub Action on self-hosted runners: supported. The Action is a thin client that posts artifact/context to the Redwood API. If you run it on a self-hosted runner within your infra, the code never touches third-party CI providers. We'll review runner config during the call.
- GitHub App scopes: typically we request metadata + pull_request + contents (read) for repo annotation flows. For a read-only annotation flow you can limit to issue_comment/pull_request and repo:status. We'll share a minimal scope manifest during the demo.

Attaching the reference GitHub Action repo and a short checklist for private repo access.

Thanks - Alex

Attachment: redwood-github-action-starter.zip (zip, 220KB)
